title: Hijack Threat Note Forces IndiGo Bengaluru-Lucknow Flight to Turn Back
excerpt: Flight 6E 451 with 178 passengers returned to Kempegowda airport after a threat note was found in the lavatory; a 90-minute search declared it a hoax and the flight later departed.
body:
• IndiGo flight 6E 451 from Bengaluru to Lucknow, carrying 178 passengers, returned to Kempegowda International Airport on Saturday after a hijack threat note was found in the aircraft's lavatory.
  • A full emergency was declared at the airport; security agencies searched the aircraft for about 90 minutes and declared the threat a hoax, a senior police officer told The Times of India.
  • The flight continued its journey to Lucknow later in the night, and an investigation is under way to identify who wrote the note.
  • If you are flying out of Bengaluru this weekend, build in extra time — a full-emergency response isolates the aircraft and can hold departures while checks run.

An IndiGo flight bound for Lucknow returned to Bengaluru on Saturday evening after a handwritten note threatening a hijack was found in the aircraft's toilet, prompting a full emergency declaration at Kempegowda International Airport. Flight 6E 451, carrying 178 passengers, had taken off from Terminal 1 at around 5:50 p.m. when the note was discovered roughly 30 minutes into the flight.

What happened on board

A passenger who entered the lavatory found the note and alerted the cabin crew, who informed the pilots. The note read, in part, "This plane is going to get hijacked exactly at 6.30," with a warning to "ignore and see the consequences," according to reports of the incident. The pilots turned the aircraft back to Bengaluru in line with standard security procedure.

"A security threat was reported onboard IndiGo flight 6E 451, operating from Bengaluru to Lucknow on 07 November 2026. In line with Standard Operating Procedure, the relevant authorities were informed immediately and the pilots decided to return to origin to carry out the necessary security checks, as per protocol."

— IndiGo spokesperson, via ANI

Search, hoax declaration and departure

On landing, the aircraft was isolated and security agencies carried out a thorough search. "We declared it a hoax after a thorough search lasting 90 minutes. Later in the night, the flight continued its journey," a senior police officer told The Times of India. No suspicious material was reported found on board.

Officials said an investigation is under way to identify the origin of the note and its author, according to ANI. Hoax threats of this kind are treated as serious offences under Indian aviation security rules even when no device or weapon is found, because the response — an emergency return, an isolated aircraft and a full search — is mandatory every time.

What travellers should know

For passengers, the practical lesson is about knock-on delays rather than safety: when a full emergency is declared, the affected aircraft is taken out of the departure sequence until it is cleared, and its onward flight leaves hours later — as 6E 451 did on Saturday night. Travellers departing Bengaluru on tight connections should check their flight status before leaving for the airport whenever a security incident is reported at the airport that day.
